title: The Boy Who Changed His Stars

pages.text: The Boy Who Changed His Stars
Long ago, in a land of castles, there lived a little boy named William. His father fixed roofs. They were poor, but they loved each other very much.
William looked at the brave knights riding by. "Father, can I be a knight one day?" His father smiled. "You can change your stars, William. You can be anything."
William grew up. He worked for an old knight, together with his two best friends, Roland and Wat.
One day, the old knight could not ride anymore. There was a big contest the next day. William had an idea. "I will ride in his place!"
William climbed on the horse. He held the long pole tight. The other knight rode fast at him. Bang! William won!
William wanted to ride in more contests. But only noble knights were allowed. So his friends helped him. They gave him a fancy new name, Sir Ulrich.
On the road, they met a funny storyteller named Geoff. He wrote the fancy papers, and he shouted William's name to the crowds.
They also met Kate, a clever blacksmith. She made William new armor. It was light and fast, and it shone like the sun.
William won again and again. But one knight did not like him. It was Count Adhemar, a proud and mean knight in black armor.
In London, William went to find his father. His father was old now, and he could not see. But he knew his son's voice. They hugged for a long, long time.
But Count Adhemar told everyone the truth. "He is not a noble! He is the son of a roofer!" The guards took William away. William did not run. He would not hide who he was anymore.
Then a man came forward. It was the Prince! William had once been kind to him. "This man is brave and true," said the Prince. "Kneel, William. Rise, Sir William!"
In the last contest, Count Adhemar played a trick and hurt William's shoulder. But William would not give up. He took off his armor, rode as fast as the wind, and won!
Everyone cheered. His friends hugged him. His father was proud. William had changed his stars. And you can change yours too. The end.
